newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak SAX index slightly up on gains to VSZ.
newsitem.headline: Slovak SAX index slightly up on gains to VSZ.

text.p: Slovak blue chips closed mixed in heavier trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Wednesday, with gains to steel maker VSZ pushing the SAX index up 0.81 points to 168.46.

Trading on the bourse's listed floor was dominated by heavy volumes in oil refiner Slovnaft and oil and gas storage company Nafta, seen by brokers as the traditional end of year tax-saving portfolio swaps.
"Most of these shares (Slovnaft and Nafta) probably changed hands in this kind of portfolio transaction," said Dusan Sykora of ING Barings.
Slovnaft traded 303,051 shares, closing down 10 crowns at 780, while Nafta closed down 50 at 1,300, on a volume of 152,245 shares.
"However, a pretty large volume of Slovnaft shares were traded on the floor, which I consider a result of the latest developments outside the bourse," he added.
The Slovak parliament on Tuesday approved a new securities law after amending it by removing several controversial paragraphs that analysts said could prove disastrous for the market.
Steel maker VSZ closed up 40 crowns at 540, helping to boost the 12-share index slightly.
Overall volume rose to 1,837,581 shares, from 721,245 shares traded on Tuesday, while turnover increased to 1.29 billion crowns, from 559.95 million.
